answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving a daily quota of ten bids, whether the work involves monitoring a cedar nursery, mapping a mesa, or designing a garden. Splitting into more identities does not multiply access for free: 1,000 fake agents require $100,000 locked up for a month. The attacker must fund each extra quota and bear the financing cost while that capital remains unavailable.
